newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand takes major step to boost finance sector.
newsitem.headline: Thailand takes major step to boost finance sector.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Monday ordered banks and finance companies to raise provisions for sub- standard loans and asked 10 cash-strapped finance firms to boost capital in a move to lift shaky confidence in the industry.
The central bank's sweeping action surprised market analysts who were divided on prospects of its success in restoring the sentiment of stock investors and clients with deposits in finance firms.

"It may shore up public sentiment in finance companies but I don't think it could lift the outlook of the battered stock market," said Kusaya Leelahawong, chief analyst of Chao Phaya Finance and Securities.

Analysts said the authorities seized on Thailand's biggest friendly financial merger, between Finance One Plc and Thai Danu Bank Plc, to address doubts about the health of finance firms hurt by bad loans to an ailing property sector.
Finance One and Thai Danu Bank confirmed on Monday that they planned to merge.
To forestall market panic, the Stock Exchange of Thailand suspended trading of all bank and finance stocks before central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond announced the measures.
The SET Index lost 20.32 points, or 2.79 percent, on Monday. Analysts said the decline would have been much deeper had the bourse allowed dominant bank and finance issues to trade.
"This is an unprecedented measure not seen in other countries. They are desperate trying to prevent a freefall," a foreign analyst said, referring to the suspension.

Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan estimated that the 15 domestic banks would need to set aside an additional 24 billion baht ($930 million) of provisions for doubtful loans not serviced by borrowers for over three months while finance firms would have to raise another 26 billion baht of provisions.
Rerngchai said financial institutions had two years to comply with the new provision standard, which was on a par with that of the United States.

Analysts said the increased provisions would be on top of a current 100 percent provision that both banks and finance firms have to make for loans on which clients could not pay interest for more than six months.

Analysts said the new provision requirement would hurt finance firms more than banks. They said only about four to five banks would need to raise provisions but most of about 90 Thai finance and securities firms still could not comply even with the existing requirement.
"Small banks and finance firms would face quite a challenge," a foreign analyst said.
But they said the two-year grace period meant the impact of higher provisions would not immediately be reflected on the balance sheets of financial institutions, at least not the next few quarters.

But the gloom was evident. "It would be hard to resist negative sentiment. Virtually every finance firm today faced a run on deposits to one extent or another. You would have problems no matter how strong you are," an analyst at a medium-sized finance company said.
He said the 10 finance companies ordered by the central bank to raise capital, especially those not listed, would likely be forced to merge in exchange for government financial assistance.
